venue.title: The venue
venue.intro: Everything you need for match day at {stadium}.
venue.sample: Sample information for this demo: the stadium and its services are fictional; the area and the metro station are real.

metro.title: Metro
metro.body: Mirpur 10 station on MRT Line 6 is a six-minute walk from gates N1 and E1. Extra trains run for two hours after the final whistle.

bus.title: Bus
bus.body: City buses stop at the Mirpur 10 roundabout, next to gate S1.

car.title: Car
car.body: Four car parks (P1 to P4) around the park open three hours before kick-off. Book a space in advance: on match days they fill up.

bike.title: Bike
bike.body: Free bike racks by gates W1 and W4.

taxi.title: Taxi
taxi.body: The drop-off and pick-up point is on the ring road by gate E3.

gates.title: Gates
gates.body: There are 20 gates: six on each long stand (S1 to S6 and N1 to N6) and four at each end (E1 to E4 and W1 to W4). Your ticket names your gate. Skybox guests use the VIP entrance.
gates.planLabel: Plan of the stadium with its 20 gates

access.title: Accessibility
access.wheelchair: Wheelchair spaces, each with a companion seat, are in row 1 of every odd-numbered block of the lower tier (101, 103, and so on).
access.entrances: Every gate has a step-free entrance, and lifts reach every tier.
access.hearing: Hearing loops at the ticket office and the information points.
access.book: Turn on “Accessible spaces” in the seat picker’s filters to see and book them.

facilities.title: Facilities
facilities.food: Food and drink on every concourse, with vegetarian and halal choices.
facilities.family: A family zone in the East stand with seats for children and a quiet room.
facilities.firstAid: First aid at every gate; ask any steward.
facilities.cashless: Card and phone payments everywhere; no cash.
facilities.wifi: Free Wi-Fi in the bowl and on the concourses.

bags.title: Bags and safety
bags.body: Bags up to A4 size are allowed and searched at the gates. Glass, cans, flares and umbrellas with points aren’t allowed.

faq.title: Questions and answers
faq.intro: Choosing seats, paying and getting in, in short.

choose.q: How do I choose my seats?
choose.a: Open a match and fly in: click a stand, then a block, then a seat. Or use the list on the right. Set how many tickets you need first: the picker only offers seats together.

view.q: Is the view from my seat real?
view.a: It’s rendered from a 3D model of the stadium, from the height and position of that exact seat, so it shows what you will see. Your ticket’s page keeps a picture of that view.

hold.q: How long are my seats kept for me?
hold.a: Ten minutes after you hold them. The countdown is in the header; when it runs out, the seats go back on sale.

max.q: How many tickets can I buy?

noWebgl.q: What if the 3D view doesn’t work on my device?
noWebgl.a: You get a 2D plan of the stadium instead, with the same blocks, rows and seats, and you can buy in the same way.

payment.a: No. This is a demo: use the test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 with any future expiry date and any security code. No money moves, and only the card’s brand and last four digits are kept.

tickets.q: How do I get my tickets?
tickets.a: Right after paying: QR tickets on the order page, a PDF to print and a calendar file. The confirmation email isn’t sent; you can read it on the order page.

lost.q: I closed the page. Where are my tickets?
lost.a: Under “Find your order”, in the same browser you bought them in. This demo keeps everything in your browser, so another browser or device can’t see them.

accessible.q: How do I book a wheelchair space?
accessible.a: Turn on “Accessible spaces” in the filters. The spaces are marked with a wheelchair symbol, and each comes with a companion seat next to it.

vip.a: Private boxes with eight lounge seats behind glass between the middle and upper tiers. From a seat view, “Upgrade to Skybox” takes you to the nearest one.

data.a: It stays in your browser. Nothing is sent to a server; clearing this site’s data in your browser deletes your orders.

legal.updated: Sample text, written for this demo.

about.title: About this site
about.body: This site demonstrates a ticket shop for a fictional stadium. The matches, prices and seats are sample data, and no tickets are actually sold.

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.body: A ticket admits one person to the seat and match printed on it, through the gate it names. Each ticket has its own QR code and can be scanned once.

prices.title: Prices
prices.body: Prices are in Bangladeshi taka (Tk) and include all taxes and fees; nothing is added at checkout.

holds.title: Holding seats
holds.body: Seats you hold are kept for you for 10 minutes. If you don’t pay in that time, they go back on sale.

refunds.title: Changes and refunds
refunds.body: If a match is cancelled, tickets would be refunded in full. Tickets can’t be exchanged for another match.

entry.title: Entry
entry.body: Gates open 90 minutes before kick-off. Bags are searched, and stewards may refuse entry to keep everyone safe.

summary.title: In short
summary.body: This demo has no server-side database. What you enter stays in your own browser, and nothing is sent anywhere.

stored.title: What your browser keeps
stored.body: Your holds, orders and tickets, the views from your seats, and the confirmation emails (which are never sent) are stored in your browser’s IndexedDB storage for this site.

card.title: Card details
card.body: The demo card form checks the number in your browser. Only the card’s brand and last four digits are kept with the order; the full number is never stored.

cookies.title: Cookies and storage
cookies.body: One cookie remembers your language. Local storage remembers the 3D picture quality and whether you have seen the opening flight, and session storage keeps an id for each open tab so the seats you hold stay yours. There are no analytics and no advertising.

deleting.title: Deleting your data
deleting.body: Clear this site’s data in your browser’s settings, and everything above is gone.

notFound.body: This page doesn’t exist or has moved.
